structure.title: Preface / Introduction
structure.summary: Document description, NASA ISS Emergency Medical Procedures Manual overview, FOIA release notes.

structure.title: Chapter 1 — Emergency Medical Procedures
structure.summary: Acute emergency algorithms and checklists: allergic reaction, CPR, AED, ALS, choking, toxic exposure, seizure, difficulty breathing.

nodes.title: 1.101 Severe Allergic Reaction (Anaphylaxis / EpiPen)
nodes.summary: Algorithm for treating severe allergic reaction or anaphylaxis on ISS. Includes epinephrine (EpiPen) administration, Benadryl, monitoring for airway compromise.

nodes.title: 1.1 — Remove Epinephrine (EpiPen) from protective plastic tubing
nodes.summary: First step: remove EpiPen from its protective plastic tubing as shown in Figure 1.

nodes.title: 1.2 — Form a fist around EpiPen with thumb closest to safety cap
nodes.summary: Grip step: form a fist around the EpiPen with thumb positioned closest to the safety cap.

nodes.title: 1.3 — Activate auto injector by pulling off safety cap
nodes.summary: Activation step: pull off the safety cap to prepare the auto injector for use. See Figure 2. WARNING: do not put fingers over needle end; do not inject through clothing.

nodes.title: 1.4 — Press needle end against outer thigh; hold for 10 seconds
nodes.summary: Injection step: using a jabbing motion, press needle end perpendicular and firmly against patient's outer thigh until a click is heard or felt. Hold firmly for 10 seconds. See Figure 3.

nodes.title: 1.5 — Discard used EpiPen; Call MCC-H to request PMC
nodes.summary: Post-injection: discard used EpiPen in original protective plastic tubing, secure with Gray Tape. Call MCC-H to request a physician medical consultation (PMC).

nodes.title: 1.6 — EpiPen may be repeated every 20 minutes if symptoms recur or progress
nodes.summary: Follow-up dosing: if allergic symptoms recur or progress, the EpiPen injection may be repeated every 20 minutes.

nodes.title: 1.102 AED-Assisted CPR
nodes.summary: Procedure for AED-assisted cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR). Covers single-rescuer and two-rescuer CPR, 30:2 compression-to-breath ratio, AED attachment and shock delivery.

nodes.title: 1.103 ALS Algorithm (Advanced Life Support / Cardiac Arrest)
nodes.summary: Advanced life support algorithm for cardiac arrest on ISS. Covers pulse check, chest compressions, defibrillation, IV/IO access, epinephrine administration, shockable vs non-shockable rhythms, return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC).

nodes.title: 1.104 AED Troubleshooting
nodes.summary: Troubleshooting guide for the Automated External Defibrillator (AED) on ISS. Lists common problems, possible causes, and corrective actions.

nodes.title: 1.105 Choking
nodes.summary: Algorithm for treating a choking crew member. Covers checking patient response, abdominal thrusts (Heimlich maneuver), back blows, unconscious patient procedure.

nodes.title: 1.106 Toxic Exposure
nodes.summary: Procedure for toxic chemical exposure on ISS. Covers decontamination, eye/skin irrigation, respiratory protection, crew evacuation considerations.

nodes.title: 1.107 Seizure
nodes.summary: Algorithm for managing a seizure (convulsion) on ISS. Covers protecting the patient, airway management, post-ictal care, medication administration.

nodes.title: 1.108 Difficulty Breathing (Respiratory Distress)
nodes.summary: Algorithm for crew member with difficulty breathing, respiratory distress, or shortness of breath. Covers airway assessment, oxygen administration, bronchodilators.

structure.title: Chapter 2 — Dental Procedures
structure.summary: Dental anatomy, examination, and emergency dental procedures for ISS crew including nerve blocks, fillings, crown replacement, tooth loss.

nodes.title: 2.6.001 Mouth Anatomy
nodes.summary: Reference diagram of mouth and dental anatomy for ISS crew medical use.

nodes.title: 2.6.101 Mouth Exam
nodes.summary: Procedure for conducting a dental and oral examination on ISS.

nodes.title: 2.6.301 Dental Procedure — Nerve Block
nodes.summary: Step-by-step procedure for administering a dental nerve block injection to manage tooth pain on ISS.

nodes.title: 2.6.302 Dental Procedure — Temporary Dental Filling
nodes.summary: Procedure for placing a temporary dental filling to manage a lost or broken filling on ISS.

nodes.title: 2.6.303 Dental Procedure — Dental Crown Replacement
nodes.summary: Procedure for replacing a lost dental crown on ISS using temporary cement.

nodes.title: 2.6.304 Dental Procedure — Exposed Dental Pulp
nodes.summary: Procedure for managing an exposed dental pulp (severe decay or broken tooth) on ISS.

nodes.title: 2.6.305 Dental Procedure — Loss of Tooth (Avulsion)
nodes.summary: Procedure for managing a knocked-out or avulsed tooth on ISS.

nodes.title: 2.6.401 Dental Treatment — Tooth Pain
nodes.summary: Decision algorithm for diagnosing and treating tooth pain on ISS.

structure.title: Chapter 3 — Medical Kit Contents and Reference
structure.summary: Complete reference for ISS medical kit contents: medications, dosages, routes of administration, side effects, and storage locations. Covers Convenience Medication Pack, IV supplies, diagnostic equipment, surgical supplies.

nodes.title: 3.001 Medical Kit — Contents and Reference (Part 1: Medications)
nodes.summary: Tables listing all medications in the ISS medical kit by category: antibiotics, antidiarrheals, antihistamines, analgesics, epinephrine, steroids. Includes strength, quantity, route, and side effects.

nodes.title: 3.001 Medical Kit — Contents and Reference (Part 2: Equipment and Supplies)
nodes.summary: Tables listing medical equipment and supplies in the ISS kit: IV supplies, oxygen equipment, AED pads, surgical instruments, diagnostic tools.
